Under the revised NCAP targets, the goal is to achieve a 40% reduction in PM10 levels by 2025 - 26, using 2017 as the base year.

This applies mainly to India's non-attainment cities.

Further Insights

NCAP was launched in 2019 by MoEFCC.

It currently covers 131+ non-attainment cities.

Targets focus on pollutants like PM10 and PM2.5.

PM10 refers to particles with diameter less than 10 microns.

Strategies include road dust control, waste burning prevention, industrial emission regulation, and improved monitoring.

MLFF aims to eliminate toll plazas and allow vehicles to move without stopping.

Part XX of the Constitution deals with "Amendment of the Constitution".

It contains Article 368, which lays down:

the procedure for amending the Constitution

the powers of Parliament to amend it

types of amendments (simple majority, special majority, and ratification)

Part XV deals with Elections (Articles 324 - 329A).

Part XVII deals with Official Languages (Articles 343 - 351).

Part XVIII deals with Emergency Provisions (Articles 352 - 360).

Further Insights

Article 368 is the core article for constitutional amendments.

India follows a rigid + flexible amendment system (neither fully rigid nor fully flexible).

Amendments needing state ratification include changes affecting federal structure (e.g., SC/ST lists, legislative powers).

Basic Structure Doctrine, established in Kesavananda Bharati (1973), limits Parliament's amending power.

Constitutional amendments can be challenged in court if they violate the basic structure.

The Ganga is NOT an antecedent river.

It is mainly a consequent and subsequent river formed after the uplift of the Himalayas and follows the natural slope of the land.

Further Insights

Antecedent rivers flow older than the mountains they cut through.

Examples include Indus, Satluj, Brahmaputra, Teesta, Arun, Kali (Sharda).

Consequent rivers form after land uplift and follow the slope (e.g., Ganga).

LIGO made history on September 14, 2015, when it detected the first-ever gravitational wave signal, called GW150914.

This was the first direct proof of gravitational waves predicted by Einstein in 1916.

Reason (R) is True

The GW150914 signal came from two massive black holes, about 29 and 36 solar masses, merging into a larger black hole.

Around 3 solar masses worth of energy was released as gravitational waves in 0.2 seconds.

This brief burst of energy exceeded the combined output of all stars in the observable universe at that instant.

Why R correctly explains A

The reason describes the exact astrophysical event that produced the GW150914 signal detected in the assertion.

Further Insights

LIGO consists of two detectors in Louisiana and Washington, USA.

Einstein predicted gravitational waves in his General Theory of Relativity (1916).

The 2017 Nobel Prize in Physics was awarded for the detection of gravitational waves.

Black hole mergers produce strong ripples in spacetime detectable across billions of light years.

India is establishing its own facility, LIGO-India, to extend global gravitational-wave detection capability.

The Punchhi Commission (Commission on Centre - State Relations) was set up by the Government of India in April 2007 - 2008 (officially constituted in April 2007, work began in 2008).

It was chaired by Madan Mohan Punchhi, former Chief Justice of India.

The Punchhi Commission recommended a fixed 5-year tenure for Governors.

It also said Governors should not be dismissed casually or at the pleasure of the Union government.

Removal should be based on objective criteria, and reasons must be recorded.

Further Insights

It suggested clear guidelines for imposing President's Rule (Article 356).

It emphasized local governments as true federal units deserving more autonomy.

It recommended creating a Permanent Inter-State Council for federal coordination.

It proposed that the role of Governors should be limited to constitutional functions, avoiding political interference.

In State of Madras v. Champakam Dorairajan (1951), the Supreme Court ruled that:

Fundamental Rights override Directive Principles, and the State cannot violate Fundamental Rights while implementing DPSPs.

This judgment led the government to pass the 1st Constitutional Amendment Act (1951) to allow reservations in education and to modify Article 15(4).

This case (1967) ruled that Parliament cannot amend Fundamental Rights.

Kesavananda Bharati vs. State of Kerala

The 1973 case established the Basic Structure Doctrine.

Minerva Mills vs. Union of India

This 1980 case said Fundamental Rights and DPSPs are complementary.

It struck down parts of the 42nd Amendment for giving DPSPs supremacy.

Further Insights

The 1st Constitutional Amendment Act (1951) introduced Articles 15(4) and 19(6).

It strengthened affirmative action policies for backward classes.

Champakam Dorairajan was one of the earliest constitutional cases tested before the SC.

DPSPs are non-justiciable, while Fundamental Rights are enforceable.

This case shaped India's early reservation and social justice policies.

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in direct speech.

The boy asked his father how old he was.
options: The boy said to his father, "How old he was?"
The boy says to his father, "How old are you?"
The boy said to his father, "How old are you?"
The boy says to his father, "How old is he?"
questions.solution:
The given sentence is an interrogative sentence, in which a boy is asking his father about his age.

The 'asked' in the Indirect speech changes to 'said to' in the Direct speech and another crucial change is the verb always comes before the subject in the Direct speech sentence.

The things that change in the Direct Speech sentence from Indirect Speech sentence are:
Indirect speechDirect speech
AskedSaid to
Old he wasOld are you

From the given options, the one that follows the above-mentioned changes correctly is option (c) "The boy said to his father, "How old are you?"" in which 'asked' is changed to 'said to', 'old he was' changes to 'old are you' and it also follows the rule of Direct Speech that "verb should precede the subject'.

Hence, the correct answer is option (c).

questions.solution:
The word "expand" means to increase in size, volume, or extent.

(a) "Enlarge" also means to make bigger and is similar in meaning to "expand".

(b) "Contract" means to become smaller or reduce in size, which directly opposes expansion.

(c) "Observe" means to watch carefully and is unrelated to size.

(d) "Delight" means to give pleasure and has no spatial meaning.

Hence, "contract" is the correct antonym of "expand", making option (b) the correct answer.

questions.question: Select the correctly spelt word.
questions.solution:
"Wierd" is incorrectly spelt. The correct spelling is "weird", which means suggesting something supernatural; uncanny or very strange.

"Vaccum" is incorrectly spelt. The correct spelling is "vacuum", which is a space entirely devoid of matter.

"Zealous" is correctly spelt. It means having or showing zeal; great energy or enthusiasm in pursuit of a cause or an objective.

"Acheive" is incorrectly spelt. The correct spelling is "achieve", which means to successfully bring about or reach (a desired objective or result) by effort, skill, or courage.

The only correctly spelt word among the options is "zealous".

Hence, option (c) is the answer.

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.

Did you guard the office last night?
options: Was the office guarded by you last night?
Were the office guarded by you last night?
Was the office be guarded by you last night?
Did the office guarded by you last night?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option (a).

The subject of the Active Voice is changed into the object of the Passive voice. Also, the object of the Active Voice is changed into the subject of the Passive Voice.

The usage of a 'to be' form of the verb is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from Active to Passive.

The preposition "by" is used before the object made in Passive Voice. However, it is optional in some cases.

The question in Active voice is an interrogative sentence. The answer to this question will be either "yes" or "no".

These types of sentences usually begin with a helping verb like "Did".

The format of the sentence which begins with "Did" in Active voice is: Did + Subject + V1 + Object?

Therefore, in Passive voice, the format will be: Was/Were + Object of the active voice (Subjective case) + V3 + by + Subject of the active voice (Objective case).

For example:

Did he beat you? (Active)

Were you beaten by him? (Passive)

The subject of the passive voice is 'office', which is singular in nature. So, the plural helping verb 'were' cannot be used here. So, option (b) is eliminated.

The options except (a) don't follow the correct grammatical format of the Passive Voice.

Thus, the correct answer is: Was the office guarded by you last night?

Note:-

Subject-Verb Agreement: Matching up singular or plural subjects with singular or plural forms of a verb is part of the process called agreement. This can be understood better by the examples given: - "She likes cooking." [singular subject and verb] -- "They like to cook vegetables." [plural subject and verb]

questions.question: Find the synonym of "Keen".
questions.solution:
The word "keen" means having a strong interest or enthusiasm.

(a) "Dull" is the opposite of "keen".

(b) "Eager" means enthusiastic or interested, which matches "keen".

(c) "Hollow" relates to structure.

(d) "Slow" relates to speed.

Thus, "eager" is the correct synonym.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the following sentence.

After presenting all the evidence, the lawyer told the jury, "The ball is in your court now."
questions.solution:
The idiom "the ball is in your court" means it is now someone else's turn to take action or make a decision. In this context, it's the jury's responsibility to decide.

a) Inaction - The idiom prompts action, not inaction.

b) Blame - Not related to assigning blame, but to the next step.

c) Disappointment - Unrelated.

d) Responsibility - Correct, as it signifies that the duty to act or decide now rests with the jury.

Hence, option (d) is the correct answer.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The homophone for the word "sail" is _______.
questions.solution:
A homophone is a word that sounds the same as another word but has a different meaning and often a different spelling.

Sail (to travel by boat using wind power) and sale (the exchange of goods for money) are pronounced the same way but have different meanings, making them homophones.

Hence, option (d) is the answer.

Seal - a marine animal or a way to close something.

Sole - the bottom of a foot or being single.

Sailor - a person who sails.

questions.question:
Fill in the blank with the appropriate preposition.

She walked ___ the room without speaking to anyone.
questions.solution: The preposition 'through' is used to indicate movement from one end of an enclosed space to the other. A room is an enclosed area, so movement within it is correctly expressed using 'through'. 'Across' is used for open or flat spaces, while 'over' [above] and 'along' [next to] do not suit the context. Hence, (b) is the correct answer.

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice.

You are requested to close all the doors of the house.
options: Close all the doors of the house.
Please close all the doors of the house.
Kindly closed all the doors of the house.
All the doors of the house should be closed by you.
questions.solution:
The subject of the Passive Voice is changed into the object of the Active Voice. Also, the object of the Passive Voice is changed into the subject of the Active Voice.

The Passive voice in this question is an imperative sentence (request).

In Passive voice, the format is: You are requested to + V1 + Object.

Thus, the format in Active voice is: V1 + Object (with "please" or "kindly").

For example:

You are requested to wash the dishes. (Passive)

Kindly wash the dishes. (Active)

The options except (b) don't follow the correct grammatical format of the Active Voice.

Therefore, the correct answer is option (b): Please close all the doors of the house.

Note: V1 -> Base form/simple form of verb, V2 -> Past form of verb (-ed form or irregular verb), V3 -> Past participle form of verb (-ed, -d, -t, -en, or -n), V4 -> Continuous form of verb / Present participle form of verb (-ing form), V5 -> Third person singular (V1+ -es or -s).

questions.question:
Choose the correct meaning of the phrase.

Go down the pan.
options: Reach a stage of abject failure.
questions.solution:
The phrase 'go down the pan' means to reach a stage of abject failure.

Usage - We don't want to see our business go down the pan.

Hence, (a) is the correct answer.

questions.question: What is the primary driver of climate change mentioned in the passage?
options: Human activities like burning fossil fuels
questions.solution:
From the following sentence in paragraph 1, "Climate change, driven primarily by human activities such as burning fossil fuels and deforestation, is profoundly altering Earth's ecosystems," it can be noted that the primary drivers of climate change are human activities like burning fossil fuels and deforestation.

Hence, the correct answer is option (d).

questions.question: How does climate change affect coral reefs, according to the passage?
options: It causes bleaching due to warmer oceans.
questions.solution:
From the following sentence in paragraph 1, "Species unable to adapt or migrate face extinction; for instance, coral reefs are bleaching due to warmer oceans, endangering marine life dependent on them," it can be noted that climate change leads to bleaching of coral reefs because of warmer oceans.

Hence, the correct answer is option (d).

questions.question: What are tropical forests experiencing due to climate change?
options: Shifts in rainfall causing habitat fragmentation
questions.solution:
As per the following sentence from paragraph 2, "Tropical forests, home to over half of the world's species, are experiencing shifts in rainfall, causing habitat fragmentation and invasive species proliferation," it can be noted that climate change has led to shifts in rainfall which in turn has led to habitat fragmentation.

Hence, the correct answer is option (b).

questions.question: What role do indigenous communities play in biodiversity conservation?
options: They advocate for traditional knowledge in strategies.
questions.solution:
As per the following sentence from paragraph 3, "Indigenous communities, often stewards of biodiverse lands, advocate for traditional knowledge in conservation strategies," it can be noted that indigenous communities voice out for traditional knowledge in conservation strategies.

Hence, the correct answer is option (a).

questions.question: What is necessary to address biodiversity loss from climate change?
questions.solution:
As per the following sentence from paragraph 3, "Addressing this crisis requires global cooperation, policy reforms, and individual actions like reducing carbon footprints to preserve the intricate web of life on our planet," it can be noted that global cooperation and policy reforms are necessary to address the crisis of biodiversity loss from climate change.

Hence, the correct answer is option (a).

questions.question: What is the meaning of the word "philanthropist"?
options: A person who collects rare stamps
A wealthy person who donates money to good causes
A person who is an expert in philosophy
A person who hoards their wealth
questions.solution:
The correct answer is b) A wealthy person who donates money to good causes.

"Philanthropist" describes a person who actively seeks to promote the welfare of others, especially by making generous donations of money to charitable organizations or good causes.

questions.question:
Rearrange the following stages in the process of judicial decision-making in a court of law in the correct order:

P. Pronouncement of the final judgment.

Q. Filing of the case and submission of pleadings.

R. Examination of evidence and arguments by both sides.

S. Interpretation of law and application to the facts of the case.
questions.solution:
Judicial proceedings begin with the filing of the case and pleadings (Q). This is followed by examination of evidence and hearing of arguments (R). The court then interprets the law and applies it to the established facts (S). Finally, the judgment is pronounced (P).

Thus, the correct order is Q → R → S → P.

Hence, option (d) is the correct answer.

questions.question:
In the following question, the first and the last parts of the sentence/passage are numbered 1 and 6. The rest of the sentence/passage is split into four parts - P, Q, R, and S. These four parts are not given in their proper order. Read the sentence/passage and find the most logical order of the parts between 1 and 6.

1: The process of photosynthesis is essential for life on Earth. P. This energy is used to convert carbon dioxide and water into glucose. Q. Green plants absorb sunlight through the chlorophyll present in their leaves. R. Oxygen is released as a by-product of this chemical reaction. S. The stored chemical energy supports plant growth and metabolism. 6: Photosynthesis, therefore, sustains both plant life and atmospheric balance.
questions.solution:
After the introduction in (1), (Q) begins the process by describing light absorption. (P) follows with energy conversion. (R) logically comes next, explaining oxygen release. (S) then highlights the benefit to plants before the concluding sentence. (6) is a concluding statement.

Thus, the correct sequence is QPRS.

Hence, option (b) is the correct answer.

questions.question: Find the synonym of "Pliable".
questions.solution:
The word "pliable" refers to something that can bend easily.

(a) "Stiff" is the opposite of "pliable".

(b) "Gentle" relates to behavior.

(c) "Flexible" means easily bent, matching "pliable".

(d) "Stern" relates to attitude.

Therefore, "flexible" is correct.

questions.question:
Choose the sentence that uses a homonym of the underlined word:

The soil in the garden was rich with nutrients for planting.
options: The billionaire lived a rich lifestyle in his mansion.
This land is rich with enormous micronutrients.
Ashok wanted to buy a land that is rich in alluvium.
The farmland's rich earth yielded a bountiful harvest.
questions.solution:
In the original sentence, "rich" is an adjective meaning fertile or full of nutrients.

Options (b), (c), and (d) use "rich" in the same sense or related to abundance/quality.

Option (a) uses "rich" as wealthy or affluent, which is unrelated to fertility.

Hence, option (a) is the correct answer.

questions.question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

The council hasn't discussed about the proposed law on taxes in parliament.
questions.solution:
In English, the verb 'discuss' doesn't need to be followed by the preposition 'about'. The verb 'discuss' means to talk about something. So, the preposition 'about' in the given sentence is redundant. So, the error is in the segment in option (d). Hence, option (d) is the correct answer.

The correct sentence is: The council hasn't discussed the proposed law on taxes in parliament.

Note:

A Preposition is a word placed before a noun or a pronoun or a noun equivalent (pronoun, adverb, gerund, infinitive, adverbial clause, or any clause that can be used as the object of the preposition) and shows a relationship in space or time or a logical relationship between two or more people, places, or things in a sentence.

Examples

1) The teacher scolded the child for being late.

2) We're going to a party.

· The words in bold are called prepositions because they normally take position before (pre) a noun/pronoun or a noun equivalent (pronoun, adverb, gerund, infinitive, adverbial clause, or any clause that can be used as the object of the preposition.

· The noun/pronoun which is used with a preposition is called its Object.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to improve the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to improve it, select 'No improvement'.

Neither Kia nor him has been able to recognize the ludicrous message.
questions.solution:
In the case of 'neither..nor', always put the verb according to the subject that is closest. In this case, 'has' (singular verb) must agree with 'he' (singular subject). So, option (b) is incorrect.

The pronoun which performs action or is the doer is called the Subjective Pronoun. In this context, the persons mentioned are performing the action and so, subjective pronouns must be used. Thus, the sentence needs an improvement and also, option (c) is incorrect as an objective pronoun is used here.

Thus, 'Neither Kia nor he has' should replace 'Neither Kia nor him has'.

Therefore, the correct answer is (a), Neither Kia nor he has.

The corrected form of the sentence is: Neither Kia nor he has been able to recognize the ludicrous message.

Additional Information:

The pronoun which takes action is called the Subjective Pronoun.

I
He
She
We
You
They

The pronoun which is the receiver of the action is called the Objective Pronoun.

Me
Him
Her
Us
You
Them

questions.question: Pick the spelling that is correct for a common natural event.
questions.solution:
The correct spelling is "Tornado." It refers to a violent rotating column of air extending from a thunderstorm to the ground. The incorrect options include extra or misplaced vowels that distort the correct pronunciation.

Hence, option (a) is correct.
